extracted.intended_audience: Program committee reviewers and area chairs for UAI 2022 (conference reviewers)
extracted.subtask_description: Instructions and evaluation criteria for reviewers and area chairs assessing submissions to the UAI 2022 conference, including required review content, scoring rubrics, confidentiality/conflict rules, and procedural guidance for discussions and rebuttals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: For each assigned paper, reviewers' main responsibilities consist of writing constructive and informative reviews, reading the author responses, participating in the discussions, and providing recommendations regarding acceptance or rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers typically assess around 4-7 papers. Respect deadlines and respond to emails promptly. Reviews may be revised as often as necessary by the reviewing deadline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Area chair responsibilities and review-quality evaluation
rubrics_metrics.description: Area Chairs typically oversee no more than 15 papers. Their responsibilities: finalize reviewer list, facilitate reviewing and discussion, summarize in a meta-review, and provide recommendation regarding acceptance or rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Area Chairs may need to closely read papers. Area Chairs will also be asked to evaluate the quality of each review using three scores: “exceeds expectations”, “meets expectations”, and “fails to meet expectations”.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality
rubrics_metrics.description: By reviewing for UAI 2022, you agree to keep all material and information confidential and use them only for the purposes of the reviewing process of UAI 2022.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not use ideas/results for your own work or distribute them until public. Delete all reviewing material (including submitted code) at the end of the reviewing cycle. Do not talk about or distribute submissions or reviewing content to anyone without prior approval from program chairs; this includes other reviewers/ACs if they may have conflicts. Primary contact regarding a submission is the assigned area chair.

rubrics_metrics.name: Double-blind reviewing / anonymity
rubrics_metrics.description: The reviewing process is double blind at the level of reviewers and area chairs (reviewers and area chairs cannot see author identities and vice versa).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors must anonymize submissions (including supplementary material). They should use third person for their own work, omit names in acknowledgements, and avoid links revealing identity. If you are assigned a submission that is not adequately anonymized, contact the corresponding area chair. Do not attempt to find out author identities (e.g., via Google or arXiv). If you accidentally discover identities, do not disclose and do not let them influence your decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflicts of interest reporting and handling
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors, Reviewers and Area Chairs will be asked to separately enter two types of conflicts into OpenReview: domain conflicts and individual conflicts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Declared conflicts are used to avoid assigning conflicted papers. If you suspect a conflict with an assigned submission, contact the area chair (or program chairs) immediately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplementary material policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Supplementary text material must be included in the same PDF as the main paper, after the references. Other supplements (code, data) must be downloaded separately from OpenReview.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Your responsibility is to read and review the main paper itself. Looking at supplementary material is at your discretion, but you may want to inspect it before criticizing a submission for insufficient details, proofs, or experimental results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Executing submitted code and following links (security)
rubrics_metrics.description: There are no guarantees about submitted code and links; running them may be unsafe.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you run supplementary source code, do so in a secure environment (e.g., Docker container, VM, or network-isolated cloud instance). Links may contain vulnerabilities or log visitor IP addresses (revealing your identity).

rubrics_metrics.name: Formatting and page-limit compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Submissions must be formatted using the UAI LaTeX template. Papers must be submitted as PDF and are limited to 8 pages including all figures and tables; at most two additional pages containing only references are allowed. Authors must not change the template.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supplementary text must follow the main paper in the same PDF (after references, starting on a new page). There is no page limit or fixed template for supplementary material. If assigned a paper that is overlength or appears to violate proceedings format (e.g., decreasing margins/font size), notify the meta-reviewer immediately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dual submissions restriction
rubrics_metrics.description: Papers under review or accepted/published in a refereed venue with proceedings may not be submitted to UAI. This also applies to substantially equal work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submitting the same or substantially equal work to another refereed venue with proceedings while under review at UAI is not allowed. Papers in conferences/workshops without proceedings, technical report repositories and arXiv are not considered dual submissions. If you suspect a dual submission, contact the corresponding area chair.

rubrics_metrics.name: Author response handling
rubrics_metrics.description: After the initial review period, authors may submit responses to their reviews to correct misunderstandings or point out missed aspects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Read each rebuttal carefully and with an open mind. Ask: Do the authors' comments change your opinion about the paper? Have you overlooked or misunderstood something? ACs encourage reviewers to acknowledge and respond to author responses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discussion period expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: There is a discussion period (two stages) involving reviewers, authors (stage 1), and later reviewers and ACs (stage 2). Discussions are important especially for borderline papers and papers with varying assessments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: At start of discussion, read other reviews and authors' response. Try to understand other points of view. Engage professionally and politely; keep an open mind. You may change your opinion, but should not give in to undue influence. Discussions are led by area chairs and full consensus is not required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Q1: Summary and contributions (review content requirement)
rubrics_metrics.description: Please summarize the paper’s motivation and key contributions in a few lines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although this may not provide much new information to authors, it is valuable to area chairs and program chairs. (Max. 500 characters.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Q2: Assessment axes (overall set)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess the work along the following axes: originality/novelty, significance/impact, soundness/technical quality, quality of experiments, reproducibility, clarity of writing, ethical considerations and resource contribution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the more detailed per-axis guidance below to assign scores; rate each axis independently where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Originality/novelty (Q2 axis and 1–4 scale)
rubrics_metrics.description: How novel are the concepts, problems addressed, or methods introduced in the paper?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 4: Excellent — main ideas ground-breaking. 3: Good — non-trivial advances over state-of-art. 2: Fair — contributes some new ideas. 1: Poor — not novel or incremental.

rubrics_metrics.name: Significance/impact (Q2 axis and 1–4 scale)
rubrics_metrics.description: How do you rate the likely impact of the paper on the UAI research community?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 4: Excellent — likely high impact across more than one subfield. 3: Good — high impact within a subfield OR moderate impact across multiple subfields. 2: Fair — moderate impact within a subfield. 1: Poor — minimal impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correctness / technical quality (Q2 axis and 1–4 scale)
rubrics_metrics.description: Is the paper technically sound?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 4: Excellent — confident technically sound, carefully checked details. 3: Good — appears technically sound, not carefully checked details. 2: Fair — minor fixable technical flaws not impacting main results. 1: Poor — major technical flaws.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality of experiments (Q2 axis and 1–4 scale, optional)
rubrics_metrics.description: If applicable, are the main claims well supported by experiments?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 4: Excellent — comprehensive evaluation, compelling results. 3: Good — adequate evaluation, results convincingly support claims. 2: Fair — weak evaluation: important baselines missing or results do not adequately support claims. 1: Poor — flawed evaluation or results fail to support claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reproducibility (Q2 axis and 1–4 scale)
rubrics_metrics.description: Are the results (e.g., theorems, experimental results) in the paper easily reproducible?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 4: Excellent — key resources (proofs, code, data) available and details comprehensively described for competent researchers to confidently reproduce results. 3: Good — resources available and details sufficiently well-described. 2: Fair — resources unavailable but key details sufficiently described for an expert to reproduce. 1: Poor — key details incomplete/unclear or resources unavailable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity of writing (Q2 axis and 1–4 scale)
rubrics_metrics.description: Is the paper well-organized and clearly written?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 4: Excellent — well-organized and clearly written. 3: Good — well organized but presentation could be improved. 2: Fair — somewhat clear but important details missing or unclear. 1: Poor — unclear and very hard to understand.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethical considerations and resource contribution (Q2 axes)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess ethical considerations and resource contributions (e.g., code/data) as part of Q2.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Flag ethical issues where appropriate (see Q10). For resource contribution, consider availability and usefulness of provided resources when rating reproducibility and impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Q3: Main strengths (review content requirement)
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe the main strengths of the work, considering the same axes as in Q2.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mention as many main strengths as there are, but avoid minor points. (Max. 1000 characters.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Q4: Main weaknesses and constructive tone (review content requirement)
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe the main weaknesses of the work, considering the same axes as in Q2.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comments should be detailed, specific, and polite. Avoid vague, subjective complaints. Do not be dismissive. If claiming the work is incremental, cite specific relevant prior work with a complete citation. If experiments are unrealistic, suggest improvements (e.g., more realistic datasets, different metrics, sensitivity analyses). (Max. 1000 characters.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Q5: Detailed comments to authors (review content requirement)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide constructive criticism and feedback that could help improve the work or its presentation (presentation suggestions, missing references, minor mistakes, typos, grammar).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include questions you want authors to clarify during the author response phase, but be specific and limit requests to points important for the decision (author responses have limited length). (Max. 200000 characters.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Q6: Overall score (10-point scale) and distribution guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide an overall evaluation of the paper, weighing reasons to accept vs reject. Use full range where appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Score options 10 (Award quality) down to 1 (Very Strong Reject) with detailed descriptions for each level. Example entries: 10 Award quality: technically flawless with groundbreaking impact, exceptional evaluation/reproducibility/resources, no unaddressed ethical concerns. 9 Very Strong Accept: technically flawless, groundbreaking impact in at least one area, etc. 8 Strong Accept; 7 Accept; 6 Weak Accept; 5 Borderline accept; 4 Borderline reject; 3 Reject; 2 Strong Reject; 1 Very Strong Reject. Calibration guidance: Ideally, no more than 25% of submitted papers in (Accept + Strong Accept + Very Strong Accept + Award Quality); no more than 20% in (Strong Accept + Very Strong Accept + Award Quality); no more than 10% in (Very Strong Accept + Award Quality); no more than 1% in Award Quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Q7: Justification for overall score
rubrics_metrics.description: Explain in a few lines how you arrived at your overall assessment, indicating which strengths/weaknesses you weighed most heavily and why.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: (Max. 500 characters.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Q8: Confidence in your score (1–5 scale)
rubrics_metrics.description: Rate your confidence in your assessment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 5: Very confident — checked all points carefully. 4: Quite confident — tried to check important points carefully. 3: Somewhat confident — chance you missed aspects, did not carefully check some details. 2: Not very confident — able to defend some aspects but likely missed key details. 1: Not confident — evaluation is an educated guess.

rubrics_metrics.name: Q9: Compliance certification
rubrics_metrics.description: I have read the UAI reviewing instructions and certify that I comply with them, in particular keep materials confidential and delete reviewing material at the end of the review cycle.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is an explicit checkbox/confirmation linking you to the confidentiality and procedural rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Q10: Ethical concerns flagging
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the submission raise potential ethical concerns (methods, applications, or data that can create or reinforce unfair bias or have a primary purpose of harm)?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Answer yes/no and provide a brief explanation if yes. This is optional. Note: overall rating should be independent of this answer; your duty is to flag papers that may need further ethical evaluation. (Max. 500 characters.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Tone and helpfulness guidance for reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviews should be constructive, detailed, specific, polite, and avoid vague or dismissive language.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Think about prior experiences receiving unfair/short/dismissive reviews and avoid repeating them. Help authors understand your viewpoint and how to improve their work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedural timeline and responsiveness
rubrics_metrics.description: Key dates for the reviewing process (submission deadline, bidding, reviewing period, discussion stages, author notification) must be observed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The schedule is tight; respect deadlines and respond to emails promptly. Reviewers should participate in both discussion stages and read/respond to author rebuttals where appropriate.
